lines: Truemed CEO Justin Mares argues most people should skip extreme biohacks and focus on a few sustainable fundamentals: better-sourced food, movement, sleep and fewer toxins.

He says US healthcare spends under 3% on prevention, so incentives only kick in after chronic disease sets in; his pitch is that HSA and FSA funds can be redirected to exercise, nutrition and sleep aids.

On diet, he claims food sourcing matters more than diet labels, blames seed oils and corn-fed poultry (high in PUFAs) for inflammation, and recommends adding collagen-rich foods like bone broth and organ meats.
He treats supplements as data-driven experiments: get blood work, run 90-180 day trials of items such as nattokinase or methylated B vitamins, then retest.
Low-cost, high-leverage habits he highlights include 30-60 minutes outdoors right after waking and passive fixes like reverse-osmosis water filters and air purifiers.
title: The Health Interventions Actually Worth Your Time | Justin Mares
